questions.q: Which window type is hinged at the top and opens outward from the bottom?
o: Hopper Window
Awning Window
Transom Window
Casement Window
questions.n: Awning windows feature top hinges that allow the sash to swing outward from the bottom, creating an 'awning' effect.

questions.q: Which window type consists of parallel glass louvers?
o: Fixed Window
Clerestory Window
Jalousie Window
Double-Hung Window
questions.n: Jalousie windows are composed of several parallel glass slats or louvers that tilt together to control airflow.

questions.q: What is a "Casement" window?
o: A window hinged at the side that opens like a door
A window built into a sloping roof
A window that is divided into many small circular panes
A window that slides horizontally on a track
questions.n: Casement windows use side hinges to swing the entire sash outward or inward.

questions.q: What is a "Friction Stay"?
o: A locking mechanism used for high-security doors
Hardware used in awning or casement windows to hold them open at a certain angle
A type of weatherstripping to prevent drafts
A lubricant used to make windows slide easier
questions.n: Friction stays provide enough resistance to keep a window sash open in a specific position against wind or gravity.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a "Pivot Door"?
o: To support very large, heavy doors that would stress traditional side hinges
To allow the door to open in both directions (double-acting)
To serve as an automatic emergency exit
To save space in narrow hallways
questions.n: Pivot hinges are mounted at the top and bottom of the door, transferring weight more efficiently than side-mounted hinges.

questions.q: Which hardware is used for "Bifold" doors?
o: Heavy-duty ball bearing side hinges
Continuous piano hinges and door closers
Magnetic latches and springs
Tracks and pivots that allow panels to fold against each other
questions.n: Bifold hardware includes a top/bottom track and specific pivot points to facilitate the 'folding' motion.

questions.q: What is a "Flush Bolt"?
o: A bolt that is visible on the surface of the door
A type of screw used for plumbing fixtures
A decorative metal cap for exposed bolts
A bolt recessed into the edge of a door to lock it into the head or floor
questions.n: It is typically used on the 'inactive' leaf of a pair of doors to secure it in place.

questions.q: What is a "Panic Bar" (or Exit Device)?
o: A reinforced metal plate to prevent forced entry
A horizontal bar on a door that opens it when pushed, used for fire exits
A handle that requires a key to open from the inside
A security alarm that sounds when the door is opened
questions.n: It allows for quick egress during an emergency by simply pushing against the bar.

questions.q: Which window is best for 100% ventilation?
o: Fixed Window
Awning Window
Double-Hung Window
Jalousie or Casement
questions.n: These types allow the entire window opening to be used for airflow, unlike sliders or double-hungs which only open halfway.

questions.q: What is a "Transom" window?
o: A window built into the floor
A window used specifically for bathroom privacy
A small window located above a door or another window
A window that is triangular in shape
questions.n: Transoms are horizontal lites placed above a door or larger window to allow in extra light or air.

questions.q: How many CHB units are needed per square meter of wall?
o: 12.5 units
20.5 units
10.0 units
15.0 units
questions.n: Given a standard CHB size of 20cm height and 40cm length, one unit covers 0.08 sqm; 1 / 0.08 = 12.5.

questions.q: Calculate the number of CHBs for a wall 4m long and 3m high.
o: 120 units
180 units
150 units
200 units
questions.n: Area = 4m x 3m = 12 sqm. 12 sqm x 12.5 units/sqm = 150 units.

questions.q: What is the standard size of a CHB?
o: 30cm x 60cm
10cm x 20cm
15cm x 35cm
20cm x 40cm (thickness varies: 10cm, 15cm, 20cm)
questions.n: The face of a standard block is 200mm high by 400mm long, with varying thickness for different wall requirements.

questions.q: What is the mix ratio for "Class A" concrete?
o: 1 : 2 : 4 (Cement : Sand : Gravel)
questions.n: This is the standard structural mix for beams, columns, and slabs in typical construction.

questions.q: What is the mix ratio for "Class B" concrete?
questions.n: Class B is slightly leaner than Class A and is often used for slabs on fill or non-critical structural members.

questions.q: How many bags of cement are needed for 1 cubic meter of Class A concrete?
o: 9 bags
6 bags
7.5 bags
12 bags
questions.n: The standard estimation for a 1:2:4 mix (Class A) is 9 bags of 40kg cement per cubic meter of concrete.

questions.q: What is the "Mortar" mix ratio for CHB laying?
o: 1 : 5 (Cement : Sand)
1 : 3 (Cement : Sand)
1 : 2 (Cement : Sand)
questions.n: This provides the necessary strength and workability for setting hollow blocks and filling joints.

questions.q: How many liters are in 1 gallon?
o: 3.785 liters
4.546 liters
3.500 liters
4.000 liters
questions.n: One US gallon is equal to approximately 3.78541 liters.

questions.q: What is the "Live Load"?
o: The weight of the concrete slab itself
The weight of the electrical wiring in the building
Temporary loads like people, furniture, and movable equipment
The load imposed by the foundation on the soil
questions.n: Live loads are transient and change over the life of the structure.

questions.q: What is the "Dead Load"?
o: The weight of the building's occupants
Permanent loads like the weight of slabs, beams, walls, and fixed equipment
The force of an earthquake on the building
The weight of snow on a roof
questions.n: Dead loads are the constant weights of the building components themselves.

questions.q: Is a "Fixed Partition" a live load or a dead load?
o: Dead Load
Live Load
Seismic Load
Dynamic Load
questions.n: Because the partition is permanently fixed and its weight constant, it is calculated as part of the building's dead weight.

questions.q: What is the standard weight of a bag of cement in the Philippines?
o: 25 kg
50 kg
40 kg
100 lbs
questions.n: Local cement bags are standardized at 40kg for general construction use.

questions.q: How many RSB ties are needed per square meter of CHB wall?
o: Depends on spacing (usually every 2 or 3 layers)
Exactly 5 ties
None, CHB walls are held together by gravity
Exactly 10 ties
questions.n: Reinforcing steel bar (RSB) ties or dowels are spaced based on engineering specifications, often every 2 or 3 block courses.

questions.q: What is the volume of a CHB core to be filled with mortar?
o: 0.1 to 0.5 cubic meters
Exactly 1 liter
Zero, cores should remain empty to provide insulation
Approximately 0.0015 to 0.003 cubic meters depending on CHB thickness
questions.n: This small volume represents the internal cavity space that must be grouted for structural walls.

questions.q: What is the "Factor of Safety"?
o: A coefficient used to calculate the price of insurance
The speed at which an elevator can safely drop
The number of workers required to maintain safety on site
The ratio of the breaking strength of a structure to the actual applied load
questions.n: It ensures the structure is designed to be stronger than the highest load it is expected to carry.

questions.q: What is "Land Use"?
o: The process of measuring the boundaries of a lot
A list of plants suitable for the local soil
The legal classification of how a piece of land can be used (Residential, Commercial, etc.)
The amount of dirt required to level a site
questions.n: Land use planning or zoning determines the allowed activities on a specific parcel of land.

questions.q: What is a "Stiffener Column"?
o: The main column that holds up the building's roof
A metal rod used to stir concrete
A small column within a CHB wall to provide lateral stability
A heavy pillar used to support a bridge
questions.n: Stiffener columns (and beams) prevent long or tall masonry walls from buckling or failing laterally.

questions.q: What is a "Screed"?
o: The process of cleaning a site after construction
A type of screw used for metal roofing
A loud noise made by a circular saw
A layer of mortar used to level a floor before the final finish
questions.n: Screeding creates a flat, level surface on top of a concrete slab to receive tiles or other finishes.

questions.q: What is "Formwork"?
o: The design phase of a project
The paperwork required for a building permit
The temporary mold into which concrete is poured
A type of decorative masonry pattern
questions.n: Formwork holds the wet concrete in the desired shape until it cures and can support itself.

questions.q: What is "Scaffolding"?
o: The process of placing the roof trusses
A type of fencing used around a construction site
The skeletal frame of a skyscraper
The temporary structure used to support workers and materials during construction
questions.n: Scaffolding provides safe access to high areas of a building for workers.

questions.q: What is a "Batten"?
o: A thin strip of wood or metal used to support roofing or siding
A tool used for smoothing wet concrete
A heavy structural beam
A type of foundation used in swampy areas
questions.n: Battens are often used to provide a mounting surface for roof tiles or to cover joints in siding.

questions.q: What is "Siltation"?
o: The accumulation of soil or sediment on a construction site, often a drainage issue
The process of making concrete more fluid
The chemical reaction of cement and water
A type of finish used for outdoor pools
questions.n: Siltation occurs when loose soil is washed away and clogs drains or nearby waterways.

questions.q: What is a "Curb"?
o: The edge where a raised sidewalk meets a street
A device that limits the flow of water in a pipe
A type of roof ridge
The base of a column
questions.n: The curb provides a physical boundary between the roadway and the pedestrian area.

questions.q: What is "Excavation"?
o: The process of removing earth for foundations
The process of building a basement wall
The process of adding soil to a site
The study of old buildings
questions.n: Excavation creates the necessary hole or trench in the ground to house the footings or basement.

questions.q: What is "Backfill"?
o: The soil used to fill in the space around a foundation after it is built
The process of revising architectural drawings
The concrete poured at the back of a retaining wall
A type of structural support for the back of a building
questions.n: Once foundations are cast and cured, backfill is placed to return the site to its intended level.

questions.q: Which tool is used to check if a surface is perfectly horizontal?
o: Chalk line
Plumb bob
Level bar
T-square
questions.n: A level bar (spirit level) uses a bubble in a liquid vial to indicate horizontal alignment.

questions.q: Which tool is used to check for vertical alignment?
o: Plumb bob
Measuring tape
Level bar
Protractor
questions.n: A weight suspended by a string uses gravity to establish a perfectly vertical line.

questions.q: What is "Tiling"?
o: The act of tilting a window for ventilation
A type of farming technique
The process of placing the first layer of soil
The process of covering a surface with tiles
questions.n: Tiling involves the installation of ceramic, stone, or glass units on floors or walls.

questions.q: What is "Grout"?
o: A type of glue used to stick tiles to the wall
The sharp edge of a broken tile
A liquid cleaner for tile surfaces
The material used to fill the spaces between tiles
questions.n: Grout is a dense fluid used to fill gaps, provide a seal, and finish the look of tiled surfaces.

questions.q: What is "Veneer"?
o: A heavy structural wall made of solid stone
A thin decorative covering of fine wood or brick
A type of glossy paint used on doors
The process of drying timber in a kiln
questions.n: Veneers are non-structural layers used to improve the appearance of a less attractive base material.

questions.q: Identify: A control valve with a round handle, usually found outside.
o: Check Valve
Gate Valve
Ball Valve
Angle Valve
questions.n: A gate valve uses a round wheel handle to raise or lower a 'gate' to stop or allow water flow.

questions.q: Identify: The pipe that extends through the roof to let gases escape.
o: Soil Pipe
Downspout
Waste Pipe
Vent Pipe
questions.n: Vent pipes allow sewer gases to bypass traps and exit the building safely through the roof.

questions.q: Identify: The large electrical box that holds all the breakers.
o: Meter Base
Panel Board
Transformer Box
Junction Box
questions.n: The panel board is the central distribution point where main and branch circuit breakers are located.

questions.q: Identify: A type of hinge that is completely hidden when the door is closed.
o: Butt Hinge
Piano Hinge
Soss Hinge (Concealed Hinge)
Pivot Hinge
questions.n: Soss hinges are mortised into the door and frame, making them invisible when the door is closed.

questions.q: Identify: The metal strip at the bottom of a door to prevent drafts.
o: Door Sweep
Threshold
Astragal
Door Stopper
questions.n: A door sweep is a flexible strip attached to the bottom of the door to seal the gap between the door and the threshold.

questions.q: Identify: A window that consists of two sashes that can slide up and down.
o: Single-Hung Window
Horizontal Slider
Fixed Window
Double-Hung Window
questions.n: Double-hung windows allow both the top and bottom sashes to slide vertically.
